text: Hey, everybody, there is no monotheism anywhere in the Bible, there is only "one God" rhetoric, which is intended to emphasize the incomparability of our God,
in comparison to the insignificance of the other gods. The texts acknowledge the existence of other gods from beginning to end,
and in certain circumstances we can demonstrate that other gods were even worshipped. Now, some folks are gonna push back and say, "No, no. That's just the apostates. That's not the faithful ones,
cause the authoritative texts say so." And I want to give you an analogy to demonstrate how misleading that is.
Let's imagine two thousand years from now historians uncover the Declaration of Independence and they read, "all men are created equal."
But they also uncover a bunch of material remains that indicate a lot of early Americans owned slaves, and didn't let women vote or own property.
Are those historians justified in saying, "Well, look at their authoritative texts. The people who wrote this obviously didn't do that.
Only the apostate Americans did that. The faithful ones believed all men were created equal"?
